title: Stitchlet curator and repairflow orchestrator
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight curator service and orchestration layer for small, composable remediation units called 'stitchlets'. Stitchlets are typed, idempotent fragments of runbooks that can be discovered, parameterized, dry-run, and executed with RBAC and audit logging. The goal is to enable first-line support and automated responders to runverified micro-remediations safely and to let higher-risk flows require approval. This ticket covers the catalog API, manifest format, catalog UI surface (console stub), telemetry hooks, and a safe execution surface with dry-run and sandbox flags.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog API accepts manifest v1 and returns typed param schema
Stitchlet execution supports --dry-run and emits deterministic telemetry events
RBAC gating: only roles with 'stitchlet.execute' can run production stitchlets
A simple console page shows searchable stitchlet catalog and example invocations
End-to-end test demonstrating a common DB connection reset stitchlet executed in sandbox mode
steps: Define stitchlet manifest schema (name, version, params, idempotency hint, preconditions, telemetry tags)
Implement catalog microservice with REST endpoints: list, read, dry-run, execute
Add a dry-run engine that validates params, simulates side effects, and returns a replayable plan
Integrate with existing runbook snippets repo and create an import pipeline for yanked fragments
Implement RBAC checks and audit logging to telemetry pipeline
Add lightweight console integration (catalog + execute modal) as a stubbed page behind feature flag
Author migration script to tag existing runbook fragments with manifest metadata
decisions: Use YAML manifest but expose JSON over the HTTP API for compatibility with SDKs
Dry-run will use a deterministic simulation layer rather than full environment mocks to avoid secret access
Telemetry events will include tokenized plan hashes for replay/debug without leaking secrets
tradeoffs: Pros: Enables safe, small-scale automation and lets support run precise fixes without full runbook execution
Cons: Adds cataloging overhead and requires discipline to keep stitchlets idempotent; potential duplicate fragments if import step is lax
